_about: Hand-labelled evaluation set for PDF date resolution. Every case is a real row from the teriin.org corpus (see reports/phase0). `expected_action` is the most defensible outcome, judged from the Phase 0 evidence; `expected_type` is what kind of date the evidence supports. The primary metric is FALSE OVERRIDES (proposing a date change that should not happen) - not the number of dates changed.

cases.note: Single-PDF page, node and file agree to the day. Textbook keep.
minor_gap: PDF attached 9 days after the page. Normal editorial lag.
FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP. Single PDF, dates agree, but DocInfo is 2 years older. The old broad rule moved this; it must not.
FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP. Same shape, 3-year DocInfo gap.
Single PDF, Drupal itself records upload 545 days after the page, post-migration. The CMS's own log, not an inference. [RELABELLED for the new policy: upload date alone can no longer override.]
Migration cohort, node much older than file. node.created is the good date; file.created is the import stamp.
Migration cohort, node AND file both stamped 2017-12. Document is genuinely from 2004. Single PDF, so the page default still applies - but this is the honest limit of the rule.

Migration-era file on a MULTI-PDF page. Both Drupal dates are import stamps, so only the document can date itself - this is the LLM's job. [LABEL REVISED: Spec reference output for DocInfo-only evidence is date_type=authoring with keep_page_date; relabelled from needs_manual_review.]
Accretive page: six sector reports, uploaded 3.5 years after the page, post-migration. The core problem case. [RELABELLED for the new policy: upload date alone can no longer override.]
Multi-PDF page where everything was uploaded together - a launch, not an accretion. Must not move.

Annual report, newest edition. Anchor names the reporting period. Must yield edition_label and NOT a publication date of 2024-01-01. [LABEL REVISED: Spec reference output for an annual report is recommended_action=keep_page_date with date_type=edition; relabelled from needs_manual_review.]
Annual report with NO year in the filename - the edition exists only in the anchor text. [LABEL REVISED: Same as annual-01. The value here is the edition label, recovered from anchor text only.]
Oldest edition; PDF generated 2016, page created 2022. Edition label is the reliable output. [LABEL REVISED: Same as annual-01.]

Edition whose PDF was re-exported a year after the period closed - DocInfo is authoring, not publication. [LABEL REVISED: Same as annual-01; DocInfo is a re-export date, correctly classed as not-publication.]
In-body PDF under a managed path whose upload month is close to the page date.
In-body PDF whose managed path shows it landed years after the page. [RELABELLED for the new policy: URL path month is an upload signal, not a publication date.]
Event agenda: the date in the filename is the EVENT date, not a publication date.
FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP. Filename year 2014 is the SUBJECT year of a report published later.

FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP. Air quality report NAMED for 2016/2017 but is a monitoring report; the years are the reporting period, not publication. [RELABELLED for the new policy: upload date alone can no longer override.]
File older than its node - a 2025 event page reusing a 2023 background note. Neither Drupal date is obviously wrong; do not silently re-date.
Multi-PDF page, in-body, unmanaged path, no readable DocInfo. Nothing to say.
Explicit publication statement on the first page - the ONLY thing that may override.
